Privacy Policy — Ramp Training

Last updated: 6 October 2026

Ramp Training is designed so your training data stays on your devices. There is no Ramp Training account, no Ramp Training server, and no analytics. Nothing you enter or that the app reads is transmitted anywhere, except:

  • the workout screen you choose to show on your own Apple Watch, Apple TV or AirPlay screen (see below), and
  • optional Game Center leaderboards, which use Apple’s service (see below),
  • a session summary, a share card or a workout you choose to copy or share yourself (see below), and
  • requests you make to Siri, which Apple handles (see below),
  • a workout you train together with others in the room, and a Fuel summary you choose to show, on your own Apple TV over your local network (see below), and
  • the number of a barcode you scan in Fuel, sent to a public food database to look the product up (see below).

What the app stores

All of the following is written to your device's local storage and nowhere else:

  • Your name, height and bodyweight entries
  • Your training history: sessions completed, exercises, sets, reps, weights used
  • Your ability estimates, attributes, level, XP and streaks
  • Your settings: equipment, units, appearance, sound preferences
  • Any discomfort you flag mid-workout: the body area and the note you write
  • Anything you log in Fuel: what you ate or drank and when, the calories and nutrition figures you entered (including caffeine and fiber), water, any daily target, and any protein, water, fiber or caffeine goal you set, and your Fuel habit level and badges. You can switch Fuel off in Options; what you logged stays on your device until you delete the app.
  • The difficulty level you choose on the free plan, and the optional name or handle you add for share cards
  • Supplements you add and when you take them, your recipes, and the foods in your pantry, including any you add from a receipt
  • Workouts you make or import
  • Your coach style and voice, figure settings, the pace and pauses you set for each exercise, and how much you pick for today's mix
  • Your Apple Watch and Health settings, and the maximum heart rate you set, if you set one
  • For each saved session, the time spent in each heart-rate zone, if your Apple Watch measured it, for the weekly zone summary in Progress

Health data

With your permission, Ramp Training reads the following from Apple Health:

  • Workouts recorded by other apps and devices
  • Active energy burned, exercise minutes and step count
  • Bodyweight, lean body mass, body fat percentage and body mass index
  • VO2 max, resting heart rate, heart-rate variability, and your heart rate during Ramp Training workouts on Apple Watch
  • Your date of birth, only to estimate your maximum heart rate for heart-rate zones
  • Sleep, including sleep stages where your watch records them, which earns an XP bonus when you have rested well and makes up the sleep report

This is used only to show your training in context and to set appropriate difficulty — for example, using bodyweight to judge movements where you lift yourself, counting workouts done elsewhere toward your conditioning, and, if you use Fuel targets, estimating how much energy a day's movement used. The sleep report works out your typical sleep times and how regular they are, on your iPhone; if you log coffee or alcohol in Fuel, it compares when you logged them with when you went to bed, also on your iPhone.

Ramp Training writes one thing to Apple Health: the workouts you finish, so they count toward your Activity rings, if you allow it and leave Save workouts to Apple Health on (Train › Options › Apple Watch and Health). Each workout is its type, its start and end, and its active energy: Ramp Training's estimate when your iPhone saves it, or the energy and heart rate your Apple Watch measured when Ramp Training on the watch recorded it. A session you end without saving is not written, and neither is a workout you log that you did elsewhere. Ramp Training leaves its own workouts out of what it reads back, so nothing counts twice.

Ramp Training never transmits health data off your devices. What it writes stays in Apple Health, which you control. You can turn off reading or writing at any time in Settings › Health › Data Access & Devices › Ramp Training, and the rest of Ramp Training will continue to work.

Music

If you use the in-workout music controls, the app reads the title and artist of what is currently playing so it can display it. This is read on the device only and is never stored by Ramp Training. While your Apple TV or AirPlay screen shows the workout, the title and artist are shown there too; nothing goes anywhere else.

Camera and photos

Ramp Training uses the camera only when you ask it to: to read a nutrition or supplement label, a grocery receipt, or a workout (written out or as a QR code), or to estimate a meal from a photo. The photo is read on your iPhone, using Apple's on-device text recognition and, for a meal, Apple's on-device image classifier, and is then discarded. It is never saved, and never sent anywhere.

If you choose a photo or a screenshot instead, you pick it in the iOS photo picker, and Ramp Training sees only the picture you pick, read the same way. From a receipt or an order screenshot, Ramp Training keeps only the foods you choose to add, not the picture, the prices or the store.

Microphone and speech recognition

Ramp Training uses the microphone only while you tap the mic in Fuel to say what you ate or drank. What you say is turned into text on your iPhone, using Apple’s on-device speech recognition, and that text fills in the log for you to check. Ramp Training does not use speech recognition that sends audio off your iPhone; where on-device recognition is not available, the mic is not offered. Neither the audio nor the text is saved or sent anywhere; only the items you choose to log are kept, in your Fuel log on your device. You can turn microphone and speech recognition access off for Ramp Training in Settings at any time.

Coach voices

Spoken cues during a workout use the voices on your iPhone. The speech is made on your iPhone, and nothing is sent anywhere to make it.

Siri and Shortcuts

You can ask Siri, or use the Shortcuts app, to log water, food or a protein scoop in Ramp Training. Siri’s handling of your spoken request is Apple’s and is covered by Apple’s privacy policy. Ramp Training receives the request on your iPhone, for example “500 ml water”, and adds it to your Fuel log there. Ramp Training sends nothing anywhere to do this.

Apple Watch and Apple TV

Ramp Training includes an app for Apple Watch, and where the Ramp Training app for Apple TV is installed, Ramp Training can show the exercise in progress on your own TV too.

Only what is on the workout screen is sent to them: the session name and workout type, the current and next exercise, its sets, reps or time, the clock, your accent colour and language; for the watch, the maximum heart rate its zones use; and for the TV, how your figure is drawn (its style, colour and pace), every block of the workout, your heart rate and the time in each zone this session if your watch measures it, the song playing, and your light or dark setting and background. Your history, bodyweight, other health data and profile are never sent. Buttons pressed on the watch or TV, including a rating or End, go back to your iPhone.

  • Apple Watch: sent directly to the watch paired with your iPhone. If you let Ramp Training save workouts to Apple Health (your iPhone asks; the watch never does), Ramp Training on the watch records the session as a workout while it runs: the watch measures your heart rate, shows it with its zone, and sends it to your iPhone to show in the player. When you save the session on your iPhone, the watch saves the workout to Apple Health; if you end without saving, it discards what it recorded. Heart rate goes only to your own iPhone and Apple Health. You can turn this off with Heart rate from Apple Watch in Train › Options › Apple Watch and Health.
  • Apple TV: only after you turn on Show on Apple TV. The workout is sent, encrypted, to Ramp Training on an Apple TV on the same local network, never through a Ramp Training server. iOS asks for local network permission the first time.
  • AirPlay or a cable: when you show your iPhone on a TV with AirPlay or a cable, Ramp Training can show the same workout board there instead of mirroring your screen (Train › Options › AirPlay screen). It is drawn by your iPhone and sent the way AirPlay sends anything; Ramp Training sends nothing itself.

App Store reviews

Now and then, after a workout that went well, Ramp Training shows Apple's own review sheet. Whether you rate the app, and what you write, goes to Apple through the App Store, not to Ramp Training.

Sharing a session summary or a share card

Ramp Training can put a summary of a session — the exercises, how you rated them, and any discomfort you flagged — onto your clipboard or into the iOS share sheet, so you can paste it somewhere yourself, for example into an AI assistant you already use. This only happens when you ask for it. Ramp Training sends it nowhere on its own: you choose the destination, and from that point the receiving app's own privacy policy governs what happens to it.

Ramp Training can also make a share card: a picture of a finished workout, a level or a badge, with a line of text and a link to Ramp Training on the App Store. The picture shows only what is on it, such as the session name, grade, minutes, calories, level, streak, and the name or handle you chose to add, if any. It is made on your iPhone when you tap Share and handed to the iOS share sheet; you choose where it goes, for example X or Messages. Ramp Training does not connect to X or any other social network or account, and sends nothing itself.

Sharing and importing workouts

You can share a workout you made or imported, as a picture with a QR code, as text, or as a file. It contains the workout's name, its exercises with their sets, reps, times and weights, and the author line if the workout came with one. It is made on your iPhone when you tap Share, and it goes only where you send it, through the iOS share sheet, AirDrop or Messages.

When you open a workout someone sends you, as a link, a QR code, a file or text, Ramp Training reads it on your iPhone and shows it to you before anything is saved. Nothing is looked up online.

Restaurant menus

Ramp Training includes nutrition figures that five restaurant chains publish for their US menus, bundled in the app. Browsing them, or logging a dish, happens on your iPhone; Ramp Training does not contact the restaurants and sends nothing anywhere. Ramp Training is not affiliated with them.

Barcode lookup

When you scan a packaged food's barcode in Fuel, Ramp Training sends only the barcode number, straight from your iPhone, to Open Food Facts (openfoodfacts.org) and, if it is not found there, to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov). As with any web request, those services can see your device's IP address. Ramp Training sends nothing else: no name, no account, no identifier, and none of your training, health or food log data. Ramp Training has no server of its own in between, and their own privacy policies cover what they do with a request.

The product name and nutrition figures they return are shown for you to confirm. A food you log, or a food you enter yourself for a barcode, is saved on your iPhone so the next scan finds it without asking anyone. The number of free scans used this week is also kept on your iPhone. Product photos are not shown or stored.

Scanning uses the camera only while the scanner is open, on the iPhone; the picture is read on the device and not saved or sent. Nutrition figures from these databases are estimates and may differ from the package.

Training together on the TV

When someone in your home joins your workout on your Apple TV, their iPhone sends the TV only the name they type for the board, a random code for that visit, and the sets they mark done. The TV passes your workout's board (the exercise, its timing and the session title) to the iPhones it has let in, and shows each person's name and sets. All of this stays on your local network, encrypted, between the devices in the room; nothing goes to Ramp Training or anyone else, and the TV keeps nothing after the session. Heart rate shown on the TV is only the host's, as before. Each person's workout is saved on their own iPhone.

Fuel on your TV

If you choose Show on TV on the Fuel screen, your iPhone sends your Apple TV a summary of your Fuel log: today's totals (calories, protein, fiber, water, caffeine and an estimate of caffeine still active), your goals, and daily totals for the last 30 days. It never sends the foods themselves. It travels on your local network, encrypted, to your own TV, and the TV keeps nothing once you switch it off or your iPhone disconnects. Anyone in the room can see what the TV shows.

Bike, treadmill and rowing machines (Bluetooth)

If you open a cardio machine screen, Ramp Training asks for Bluetooth permission and reads your bike, treadmill, rowing machine or heart-rate strap directly over Bluetooth: speed, cadence, power, resistance, incline, distance and heart rate. It only reads; it never changes the machine's speed, incline or resistance. While a session is open it can keep reading with the iPhone locked (Bluetooth background mode). Without an Apple Watch, iOS 26 and later can record the session on the iPhone itself, with heart rate from sensors Apple Health can read during it (such as compatible AirPods). A Live Activity shows the session on your Lock Screen. These readings, your finished sessions, your goals and the name of the device you last used stay on your iPhone. A session you save goes to Apple Health as a workout. Nothing is sent to us or anyone else.

Medicines log (GLP-1)

If you use the GLP-1 log, Ramp Training stores what you enter: the medicine name, dose, date, injection site, side effects you note, your supply, refill dates and shipment tracking numbers. It stays on your iPhone, encrypted with the rest of your training data, and is never sent to us. Ramp Training doesn't look up shipments; Track opens the carrier's own website in your browser. Reminders are local notifications scheduled on your iPhone, and the optional dose-day alarm is scheduled on your iPhone with Apple's AlarmKit. A report you export as a PDF is only shared where you choose to send it. Ramp Training does not give medical advice or suggest doses.

Apple Intelligence estimates

If you tap Estimate with Apple Intelligence in Fuel, the foods Ramp Training didn't recognise are estimated by Apple's on-device model. It runs on your iPhone; Ramp Training doesn't use Apple's cloud model for this, and nothing is sent to us. You review the estimates before they're logged.

Medications from Apple Health

If you choose Import from Apple Health Medications in the GLP-1 log, Apple Health asks which medications Ramp Training may read. Ramp Training reads the doses you logged as taken for those medications and adds them to the GLP-1 log on your iPhone. It doesn't write medications to Health.

Age range

When you first open Ramp Training on iOS 26 or later, it may ask Apple whether you're 16 or over, using Apple's Declared Age Range. Ramp Training gets only a yes or no age band, never your birthdate, and doesn't store it.

Face ID lock and discreet mode

If you turn on the lock in Privacy, iOS checks Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode and tells Ramp Training only whether it passed. Ramp Training never sees or stores biometric data. Discreet mode changes the wording of reminders and cards on your iPhone; it sends nothing.

Writing to Apple Health

Besides saved workouts, Ramp Training writes to Apple Health, with Health's permission: weight you log in Ramp Training (unless you turn it off in Privacy), how hard a workout felt (Apple's effort score), and food and water you log, only if you turn that on.

Health records and clinician plans

If you tap Suggest from my health records or Fill from my health records, Apple Health asks whether Ramp Training may read your conditions, procedures and medications from the clinical records you've connected to Health. Ramp Training uses them on your iPhone to suggest areas to protect or a GLP-1 medicine; it applies only what you choose and doesn't keep the records. A plan from your physio arrives as text, a QR code or a file you open; the visit summary is a PDF made on your iPhone and shared only where you send it. Nothing is sent to us or to your clinician by Ramp Training.

Game Center (optional)

If you use leaderboards or friends features, Ramp Training uses Apple Game Center. That is optional and only starts when you open Friends and sign in with Game Center on your device.

Once you have, Ramp Training reconnects to Game Center each time it opens and posts your level, weekly streak and total XP after each workout, so your scores stay current. “Keep my scores up to date” on the Friends screen turns this off; Ramp Training then stops posting and stops reconnecting.

Apple may receive your Game Center display name and the scores Ramp Training submits (level, streak and total XP). Ramp Training does not send your training history, bodyweight, health data, or profile to Game Center — only the scores for boards you use. Game Center is operated by Apple under Apple’s privacy policy; Ramp Training does not run a separate social server.

You can ignore Game Center entirely. The rest of Ramp Training works without it.

What is not collected

  • No Ramp Training account, email address or Ramp Training sign-in
  • No advertising identifiers and no tracking across apps or websites
  • No analytics, crash reporting or usage telemetry from Ramp Training
  • No data shared with advertisers or data brokers

Aside from optional Game Center (Apple), the workout screen on your own Watch, TV or AirPlay screen, and what you choose to share yourself, such as a share card or a workout, training data does not leave your devices. Barcode lookup sends only the barcode number, as described above.

Deleting your data

Deleting Ramp Training from your device permanently removes everything it has stored locally, including your training history and your Fuel log. There is no Ramp Training copy on a server, so this cannot be undone. Scores already posted to Game Center remain under Apple’s Game Center until you remove them there, and workouts Ramp Training saved to Apple Health stay in Apple Health until you delete them there.

Children

Ramp Training is for people aged 16 and over. It is not directed at children and does not knowingly collect information from anyone under 16.

Not medical advice

Ramp Training provides general fitness information. It is not medical advice and is not a substitute for a physician, physiotherapist or qualified trainer. Consult a professional before starting a new exercise programme, and stop if you experience pain. The full fitness disclaimer, assumption of risk, and liability terms are in the Terms of Use bundled with the app. Fuel is a log of the numbers you enter and typical values you can change, including estimates from a meal photo and figures restaurants publish; it is not dietary advice, and the protein and water goals are numbers you choose. Ramp Training does not recommend supplement doses; follow the label or your doctor. Talk to a doctor or a registered dietitian before changing how you eat. The sleep report describes your sleep and suggests general habits; it does not diagnose anything. If you snore loudly, stop breathing or gasp in your sleep, or are very sleepy during the day, talk to a doctor. Heart-rate zones use a general estimate of your maximum heart rate unless you set your own; they are not medical advice.
